review_evidence: Line-start declaration grep over all 69 files: minimum count 1; files with count 1 are HexBasic/ListShim.lean and the 8 hex-primality-compact-primecert files.

reports/bench-results/hex-primality-compact-primecert/Curve25519.lean and Curve448.lean: each states and proves `theorem result : Nat.Prime (2 ^ 255 - 19)` / `Nat.Prime (2 ^ 448 - 2 ^ 224 - 1)` using prime_cert% Pocklington certificates.

reports/bench-results/hex-primality-compact-primecert/family-{31,61,123,256,511,512}.lean: each proves `theorem result : Nat.Prime <n>` in namespace PrimeCert.Comparator.BitN with a prime_cert% certificate (for example family-31 proves 2147483647 is prime).
HexBasic/ListShim.lean: proves `List.nodup_subset_length_le` by induction, a nodup-subset length bound.
reports/scratch/FactorDemo.lean and GcdProbe.lean: define ZPoly helpers, a ZMod64.Bounds 13 instance, and `main` that factor or take gcds of integer polynomials through Hex.factor and DensePoly.gcd.

reports/bench-results/dyadic-cancellation/before.Basic.lean and after.Basic.lean: define `Hex.DyadicInterval` and dyadic Horner evaluation; they differ from each other in the evaluation body, so each version is distinct content.

reports/bench-results/dyadic-cancellation/RealRoots.Bench.lean and Sturm.Bench.lean are SHA-256 identical to bench/HexRealRoots/Bench.lean and bench/HexSturm/Bench.lean; per docs/CORPUS-FILTERING.md section 4 duplicate collapse must keep path aliases searchable, so they are retained here.
summary: Surveyed all 69 listed .lean files (49 library files under Hex*/, 12 under reports/bench-results/, 8 under reports/scratch/) by size and by a line-start grep for theorem/lemma/def/structure/class/instance/inductive/abbrev/example/axiom/opaque/macro/syntax/elab/notation with optional private/meta/noncomputable/partial modifiers. Every file had at least one declaration match (minimum 1). Read completely the 12 lowest-count or smallest files: all 8 reports/bench-results/hex-primality-compact-primecert/*.lean, HexBasic/ListShim.lean, reports/scratch/FactorDemo.lean, reports/scratch/GcdProbe.lean, and the diff between the two dyadic-cancellation Basic snapshots. Each holds formal content: primality theorems, a proved list lemma, or defs over Hex polynomial APIs. SHA-256 comparison shows RealRoots.Bench.lean and Sturm.Bench.lean are byte-identical to bench/HexRealRoots/Bench.lean and bench/HexSturm/Bench.lean, but docs/CORPUS-FILTERING.md section 4 requires exact-duplicate collapse to keep path aliases searchable, which the pipeline handles through exact-duplicate metadata, not a repository-review blacklist. No file meets the FILTER-002/FILTER-004 bar, so the unit is retained in full.
